info: Rutherford's atomic model was developed from the results of the gold foil experiment. In the experiment, positively charged alpha particles were directed at a very thin sheet of gold foil. Most alpha particles passed straight through, showing that most of the atom is empty space. Some particles were deflected, and a very small number were deflected through large angles or scattered backward. From these observations, Rutherford concluded that an atom has a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus at its center, with electrons outside the nucleus.

questions.questionText: What did Rutherford conclude when most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil?
options: Most of the atom is empty space
The atom has no charged particles

questions.questionText: What did the deflection of some alpha particles indicate?
options: Positive charge is concentrated in a small region
All particles pass through atoms unchanged
Electrons form the center of the atom

questions.questionText: What is located at the center of Rutherford's atomic model?
options: A tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus

questions.questionText: What happened to a very small number of alpha particles in the gold foil experiment?
options: They were deflected through large angles or scattered backward
They disappeared inside the gold foil
